description: The complete registry of workload archetypes. Each archetype defines a workload pattern (implementation-agnostic) and the AWS services that can serve it. Used for: (1) classification — matching a source resource to an archetype by its description, (2) candidate generation — listing possible AWS targets for CONSTRAIN → RESOLVE.

container.description: Long-running or request-driven workloads packaged as containers. Includes HTTP APIs, background workers, web apps, and orchestrated container deployments. The workload runs continuously or responds to requests — it is not purely event-triggered and short-lived.

function.description: Short-lived, event-triggered execution units. Triggered by events (HTTP, queue, schedule, file upload) and expected to complete within minutes. Stateless, scales to zero, billed per invocation.

vm.description: Full operating system workloads requiring direct OS access, specialized hardware (GPU), custom kernels, or Windows. Always-on compute that cannot be containerized or runs legacy software.

relational-db.description: SQL databases: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, MariaDB, Oracle. Structured data with ACID transactions, relational schema, SQL query interface.

nosql-document.description: Document or key-value stores with flexible schema. Optimized for high-throughput reads/writes on individual items. No relational joins.

cache.description: In-memory data stores for caching, session management, or real-time leaderboards. Sub-millisecond latency, ephemeral or semi-persistent.

distributed-relational.description: Globally distributed SQL databases requiring strong consistency across regions. Multi-region writes with linearizability guarantees.
